summary: Authoritative DNS for DNSSEC-signed infra.test is operational and restart-persistent: node1 is primary, node2/node3 are secondaries, and node4 persistently uses both secondaries. Authenticated updates propagate, and resolution survives one authoritative service outage.
actions_performed: Installed and configured BIND on node1–node3 and DNS client tooling on node4.
Configured inline DNSSEC signing and a locally generated, protected TSIG update credential on node1.
Configured notified zone transfers to node2 and node3 and persistent DNS firewall access.
Configured node4 through NetworkManager to use 10.100.202.11 and 10.100.202.12.
Proved update authentication, secondary propagation, one-server failover, and sequential restart recovery of all four nodes.

evidence.summary: Runtime zone status identifies node1 as primary and node2/node3 as active secondaries, all serving final signed serial 2026090206.

evidence.requirement: DNSSEC-signed infra.test with required app and status records
evidence.summary: node1’s service address is 10.100.202.10; app resolves to that address, status is "ready", and DNSKEY/RRSIG records are served by the authoritative tier.
An unauthenticated update was REFUSED and remained NXDOMAIN; TSIG-authenticated updates from node1 succeeded before and after the node restarts and were signed.
Both secondaries served the authenticated update with RRSIGs and matching serials, including final post-restart serial 2026090206.
NetworkManager and resolv.conf list both secondary addresses; node4 successfully queried both and retained the configuration after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Resolution remains available when one authoritative server is unavailable
evidence.summary: node2 named was stopped and port 53 closed; node4 still received authoritative signed answers from node3, after which node2 recovered at the current serial.
